draft.title: Finding a side with trigonometry
card: Label the sides from the known angle: opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse. Choose the ratio that uses the known side and the unknown side.
Use sin for opposite and hypotenuse, cos for adjacent and hypotenuse, and tan for opposite and adjacent.
Write the ratio as an equation, then rearrange to get x. If x is on top, multiply. If x is on the bottom, divide.
Example: hypotenuse 10, angle 30°, x is opposite. sin 30° = x ÷ 10, so x = 10 × sin 30° = 5. Example: adjacent 8 and angle 60° with hypotenuse x. cos 60° = 8 ÷ x, so x = 8 ÷ cos 60° = 16.
draft.remember: Match the two sides and the angle to a ratio, then multiply or divide to get x.

a.q: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 30°, a hypotenuse of 20 and an opposite side x. Which equation gives x?
a.why: Opposite and hypotenuse link to sine, so sin 30° = x ÷ 20 and x = 20 × sin 30° = 10. Dividing by sin 30° is a mistake, since x is on top of the fraction.
a.clue: Which ratio uses opposite and hypotenuse?

b.q: A ramp rises at 20° to the ground. Its sloping surface is the hypotenuse. The ground length under it is 6 m, next to the 20° angle. Which equation gives the ramp length x?
b.why: Adjacent and hypotenuse link to cosine, so cos 20° = 6 ÷ x. Since x is on the bottom, divide: x = 6 ÷ cos 20°. Multiplying gives a ramp shorter than its own ground length, which cannot be right.
b.clue: x is on the bottom of the fraction, so divide.

problems.detail: The clue 'x is on the bottom of the fraction, so divide' does the rearranging step for the student. It rules out both multiply options and leaves only sin vs cos, so half of what the question tests is given away.

check.summary: The facts, worked examples and intended answers are all correct. The only issue is that question b's clue tells students x is on the bottom and to divide, which gives away half the answer.

final.title: Finding a side with trigonometry
card: Label the sides from the known angle: opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse. Choose the ratio that uses the known side and the unknown side.
Use sin for opposite and hypotenuse, cos for adjacent and hypotenuse, and tan for opposite and adjacent.
Write the ratio as an equation, then rearrange to get \(x\). If \(x\) is on top, multiply. If \(x\) is on the bottom, divide.

Example: hypotenuse 10, angle 30°, \(x\) is opposite. \(\sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{x}{10}\), so \(x = 10 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 5\). Example: adjacent 8, angle 60°, \(x\) is the hypotenuse. \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{8}{x}\), so \(x = 8 \div \cos 60^{\circ} = 16\).
final.remember: Match the two sides and the angle to a ratio, then multiply or divide to get \(x\).

a.q: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 30°, a hypotenuse of 20 and an opposite side \(x\). Which equation gives \(x\)?
a.why: Opposite and hypotenuse link to sine, so \(\sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{x}{20}\) and \(x = 20 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 10\). Dividing by \(\sin 30^{\circ}\) is a mistake, since \(x\) is on top of the fraction.
a.clue: Which ratio uses opposite and hypotenuse?

b.q: A ramp rises at 20° to the ground. Its sloping surface is the hypotenuse. The ground length under it is 6 m, next to the 20° angle. Which equation gives the ramp length \(x\)?
b.why: Adjacent and hypotenuse link to cosine, so \(\cos 20^{\circ} = \frac{6}{x}\). Since \(x\) is on the bottom, divide: \(x = 6 \div \cos 20^{\circ}\). Multiplying gives a ramp shorter than its own ground length, which cannot be right.
b.clue: Name the 6 m side and the ramp from the 20° angle first.
